The church of Eris rose like a tide. For three centuries after the false goddess's staged departure, the Erisian faith converted, conquered, and crusaded its way across Erisdar. Holy orders marched beside imperial legions. The Pontificate of Eris was established. Conversion or conquest — total influence if not total control. The Shadows believed their plan was finally back on track. The Church would provide the ideology, the Empire would provide the sword, and together they would finish what Baoth had failed to do: unify all of Ge'or under a single hand.

They did not know the Glorious Alliance reactor was about to fail.

Deep beneath the earth, the ancient machinery of the crashed ship — fifteen thousand years old, never properly shut down — finally broke. In Year 0, the reactor malfunctioned. The Great Divergence reshaped the world. The land itself convulsed; the old maps died; Elvengar was destroyed in a single cataclysm, and something new — something the Shadows had never planned for — stirred in the wreckage.

Everything they had built was thrown into chaos. The Church survived — it was too deeply rooted by then — but the perfect world they had engineered had cracked. And it would have to be rebuilt, century by century, in an age they no longer controlled.

The Erisian Era ended on the day the reactor failed. The Age of Divergence had begun.
